title: clip.v1
$comment: A reader-derived public projection over the immutable before/after blobs of a file.changed event. It is NOT a log event and is never appended; it is a pure function of (before bytes, after bytes, projection_version), computed on demand and cached disposably. Spans reference the raw blob bytes by zero-based half-open byte offsets; a null span means NO corresponding span on that side (created/deleted content), never unreadable content. Unreadable/gone content is a non-ready status or a per-side `unavailable` method, each with an explicit reason. `projection_version` names the complete algorithm and is the cache key. Unknown fields permitted for forward compatibility.

change_seq.$comment: The `seq` of the file.changed event this projection is derived from. Stamped on the response; never part of the cache key.

projection_version.$comment: Names the complete extraction algorithm and is the cache key. A dropped cache recomputes an identical result under the same version.

status.$comment: `ready` = function-level clips (reserved for a later version). `fallback` = a diffable file rendered as changed byte ranges. `skipped` = no bounded clip could be produced (binary/oversize/no-change/etc.). `unavailable` = a referenced blob's content is gone or was never captured.

fallback_reason.$comment: Required for every status except `ready`. Explains why the projection is not `ready` (e.g. `function-extraction-unavailable`, `timeout`, `overloaded`, `binary`, `oversize`, a snapshot/blob reason).

span.$comment: null means NO corresponding span on this side (created/deleted content), never unreadable content.

method.$comment: `changed-range` = a real diff hunk. `whole-file` = the side could not be diffed (create/delete/diff-too-large/before-unavailable). `absent` = the path did not exist on this side. `unavailable` = the side's content is gone or was not captured.

reason.$comment: Present when the method needs one (e.g. `unavailable` carries the blob/snapshot reason).

byte_start.$comment: Zero-based inclusive start byte offset into the raw blob.

byte_end.$comment: Zero-based exclusive end byte offset; the span is [byte_start, byte_end). Always lands on a UTF-8 boundary.

line_end.$comment: 1-based inclusive last line covered. Lines split on \n (0x0a); a preceding \r stays in the line (CRLF preserved); a trailing newline does not create a phantom last line.

truncated.$comment: True when the per-side line/byte budget clipped this span short of the full changed range.
